title: Kernels and cokernels of coherent modules on locally Noetherian algebraic spaces
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $X$ an algebraic space over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], locally Noetherian on etale scheme charts [pqf-def-locnoeth]. Modules and quasi-coherence are on the small etale ringed site [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module]. A module is coherent when it is quasi-coherent and its pullback to every etale scheme chart is coherent [pqf-def-coherent]. The kernel and cokernel, in module sheaves, of any morphism of coherent $\mathcal O_X$-modules are coherent. The zero module, every finite direct sum of coherent modules, and every extension of coherent modules are coherent.

source.place: Tag 07UC, lemma-coherent-abelian-Noetherian, statement and proof; finite direct sums are split extensions and the zero module is coherent by Tag 07UB, lemma-coherent-Noetherian.

proof.text: First compare the two formulations of coherence. On a locally Noetherian scheme chart $T$, [pqf-lem-coherent-ft-locnoeth] says that a scheme module is coherent exactly when it is quasi-coherent of finite type. By [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-finite-type-affine], finite type is equivalent to finite generation of sections on affine opens; [lem-weil-pbc-affine-tilde-gamma-adjunction](3) identifies each such quasi-coherent restriction with the tilde sheaf of its section module. Under [lem-trf-scheme-zariski-etale-quasi-coherent-equivalence], a scheme quasi-coherent module corresponds to its tensor-sections sheaf: on an affine etale map $\operatorname{Spec}B\to\operatorname{Spec}R$, the sheaf associated to $N$ has value $B\otimes_RN$, by [lem-weil-pbc-tilde-pullback-base-change] and [lem-weil-pbc-spec-module-tilde-sections] (the latter at $D(1)$). Thus the affine-chart predicate used in [lem-sfb-space-coherent-kernel-cokernel-extension] is precisely the chartwise coherence predicate in this item. Conversely these affine descriptions give quasi-coherent Zariski modules by [pqf-def-coherent], coherent by the same finite-type criteria, and also imply site quasi-coherence: locally on every chart they are associated-module sheaves, hence have the free presentations of [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module]; the same presentations on these covering slice sites give quasi-coherence on $X$. This comparison concerns module sheaves themselves, not merely their groups of global sections.

source.place: Tag 07UB, lemma-coherent-Noetherian, together with coherent.tex Tag 01XZ, properties.tex Tag 01PB, and descent.tex Tag 03DX(2).

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-space-coherent-kernel-cokernel-extension] with $Z=X$. Its base is an arbitrary scheme $S$, its local Noetherian condition is the same condition on etale scheme charts, and its kernels, cokernels and short exact sequences are in the same small-etale category of $\mathcal O_X$-module sheaves. With the predicate identified in step 1, its zero-module assertion gives the zero clause; its assertion for every morphism gives both the kernel and the cokernel clauses; and its assertion for $0\to F\to E\to G\to0$ gives the extension clause. No quasi-coherence assumption on $E$ is added.

source.place: Tag 07UC, lemma-coherent-abelian-Noetherian, reused through the existing DAG theorem, with Tag 07UB for zero.

proof.text: For coherent $F,G$, form the finite direct sum sheaf $F\oplus G$ sectionwise. The maps $a\mapsto(a,0)$ and $(a,b)\mapsto b$ give $0\to F\to F\oplus G\to G\to0$: the kernel of the projection is exactly the pairs $(a,0)$, and $b\mapsto(0,b)$ is a section of the projection. Hence the extension assertion of [lem-sfb-space-coherent-kernel-cokernel-extension] makes $F\oplus G$ coherent. Induction on the number of summands, with the zero module as the empty sum, proves the finite-sum clause.

source.place: Tag 07UC, extension assertion applied to the explicitly split sequence; finite induction, with zero from Tag 07UB.

lean.statement: theorem coherent_kernel_cokernel_zero_finite_sum_extension {S : Scheme.{u}} (X : AlgebraicSpace S) (hln : ∀ T : X.EtaleSite, IsLocallyNoetherian (X.etaleForget.obj T)) : (∀ (F G : X.Modules) (f : F ⟶ G), F.IsFinitePresentation → G.IsFinitePresentation → (∀ k : KernelFork f, IsLimit k → k.pt.IsFinitePresentation) ∧ (∀ c : CokernelCofork f, IsColimit c → c.pt.IsFinitePresentation)) ∧ SheafOfModules.IsFinitePresentation (⊤_ X.Modules) ∧ (∀ (I : Type v) [Finite I] (F : I → X.Modules), (∀ i : I, (F i).IsFinitePresentation) → ∀ b : Bicone F, b.IsBilimit → b.pt.IsFinitePresentation) ∧ (∀ c : ShortComplex X.Modules, c.ShortExact → c.X₁.IsFinitePresentation → c.X₃.IsFinitePresentation → c.X₂.IsFinitePresentation)
lean.note: Coherence is the existing Mathlib IsFinitePresentation predicate, equivalent to site quasi-coherence and coherent scheme-chart pullbacks by Stacks 07UB, on the locally Noetherian spaces in this statement. Kernels, cokernels and finite sums are quantified by their universal properties in all module sheaves. The terminal module is the zero module. No extra global sheafification instance or arbitrary replacement category is assumed.
